summary: Iteration_4 (Reviews) tested end-to-end. Backend pytest: 12/12 NEW Iter4 review tests pass (happy 5★ path with reward+credit increment, 3★ no-reward+public=false, rating 0/6 → 422, /public/review-info success + 404, featured-reviews filter & PII stripping, list/moderate/delete auth+admin enforcement, dashboard avg_rating/review_count/pending_reviews, /public/review rate-limit 429). Frontend Playwright: ALL 6 review flows verified — public /review/{token} 5-star happy path (heading 'Hey TEST_FE_ReviewA ✦', stars + comment, submit-disabled-at-0, success card with filled stars + ₹50 reward coupon THANKS-XXXX + Copy + WhatsApp share), already-submitted view ('you've already shared 5★ for this visit', form removed), /book featured-reviews section (3 cards with star row + comment + customer name), admin dashboard rating-widget (4.5 · 20 reviews) + pending-reviews-widget (0), admin /reviews page (avg-rating-value=4.5, distribution bars, 4 filter tabs all/5/4/1-3, 20 toggle + 20 delete buttons), Appointments page send-review button shown only on completed appts (1 button for the 1 completed appt; scheduled appts show none). Pre-existing TestInvoices flake (pytest-xdist race) still present but unrelated to Iter4.

minor.issue: Pre-existing pytest-xdist parallel-worker race ('Invalid customer'); flagged in iteration_3 — not an Iter4 regression.

issues: Uses browser-native <input type='date'> (07/02/2026) instead of shadcn calendar component. Acceptable but inconsistent with design system if shadcn is the standard.

action_items: (LOW) Consider replacing native date input on Appointments page with shadcn Calendar/Popover for design consistency.
(LOW) Pre-existing TestInvoices flake under pytest-xdist still untouched (iter3 carry-over).
critical_code_review_comments: REVIEW reward code uses secrets.token_urlsafe(3).upper().replace('_','X').replace('-','Y')[:5] — guarantees 5-char alphanumeric output and is safe (5^char ~36-base entropy). OK.

POST /public/review/{token} rate-limit (10/10min) is evaluated BEFORE 404/duplicate check — correct (prevents enumeration). But because it shares the same in-memory _RATE_BUCKET as /public/book (different key_suffix), bucket grows unbounded; consider a TTL sweep to avoid memory creep in long-running processes.
/api/reviews list endpoint is auth-gated via Depends(get_current_user) but NOT admin-only — any staff can read all customer comments. Consider role-gating if PII (customer_name) is sensitive.

Featured-reviews endpoint correctly strips customer_id, appointment_id, staff_id, reward_code; however customer_name is still returned in plaintext. Acceptable for testimonials but flag for privacy review.
DELETE /api/reviews/{id} returns nothing on a missing id (delete_one is idempotent) — would be cleaner to 404 if not found, otherwise admin UI can never tell if a stale id existed.

pending_reviews calculation = completed_appts - review_count is per-appointment fair, but if some completed appts already have reviews while others don't, the math still works only because there's a unique-per-appointment constraint enforced by the duplicate-check. OK.

rca of the issue: No bugs to RCA. Initial test helper bug (KeyError 'customer' from public/book response shape) fixed by switching to authenticated /api/appointments admin path which (a) returns the appointment directly and (b) bypasses the per-IP /public/book 8/10min rate limit — that limit was masking review-test setup when running concurrently with iter3 booking tests. Initial rate-limit test failure was because only 8 appts could be created (book limit), then only 8 reviews submitted — needed to flip the test to hit the review endpoint directly with a dummy token to exercise the 10/10min limit without dependency on appt creation. Both fixed and now stable across multiple runs.
